newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures dive on EMU worries, technical break.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures dive on EMU worries, technical break.

text.p: Bund futures posted one of their biggest declines in weeks on Monday as uncertainty about European monetary union and technical factors sparked heavy selling.
The June DTB Bund futures contract was down 79 basis points in late trade at 100.67 after having traded in a broad band between 100.59 and 101.60.

Analysts said comments from Finance Minister Theo Waigel suggested on balance that Germany may be willing to interpret Maastricht Treaty criteria loosely despite constant calls from the Bundesbank for the goals to be strictly met.
Waigel told the Bild newspaper that meeting Maastricht criteria was more important than sticking to the planned launch date in 1999.

But speaking to reporters in Brussels, he said that a strict interpretation still allowed special factors to be taken into account -- seeming to open the door for a fudge of Maastricht goals, even if only on the debt target.
"We are starting to see a risk premium be really factored in to Bunds," said Catherine Lee, analyst at R.H. Wrightson and Associates in London.
Traders in Germany downplayed the EMU worries, saying comments such as those heard today were only part of what will be a long-running debate on the euro.
Indeed, Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister in Vienna called for a strict interpretation of the fiscal deficit criteria of the Maastricht Treaty.

They said technical factors were largely responsible for the decline. The Bund future has broken trend line support dating back to the middle of June which has acted as a support level in September and around the turn of the year.

Rate jitters also pulled U.S. Treasuries down, contributing to the Bund market's weakness. Bunds underperformed U.S. debt, however, with the spread narrowing to 107 basis points from 110 basis points at the previous close.
The German yield curve widened steeply on the day with the spread between two- and 10-year maturities climbing seven basis points to 217 basis points.
